DECISION AND OPINION ON REVIEW 
Timely Petition for Review under §19(b)/8(a) having been filed by Respondent herein and 
notice given to all parties, the Commission, after considering the issues of causal connection, 
medical expenses, and prospective medical care, and being advised of the facts and law, changes 
the Decision of the Arbitrator as stated below, and otherwise affirms and adopts the Decision of 
the Arbitrator, which is attached hereto and made a part hereof.   The Commission further remands 
this case to the Arbitrator for further proceedings for a determination of a further amount of 
temporary total compensation or of compensation for permanent disability, if any, pursuant to 
Thomas v. Industrial Commission, 78 Ill.2d 327, 399 N.E.2d 1322, 35 Ill.Dec. 794 (1980). 
The Commission affirms the Arbitrator’s finding that Petitioner proved causation of his 
current bilateral shoulder conditions and need for the prospective medical care recommended by 
Dr . Lawarence Li, based upon Petitioner’s testimony, the medical records, and Dr. Li’s opinions, 
which we also find are more persuasive than those of Dr. Cohen.   
The Arbitrator also concluded, in the second to last paragraph on page 10 of the Arbitration 
Decision, that the “chain-of-events also support a finding of causal connection.”  However, we 
find there were factual errors in that paragraph.  Given our finding that the evidence and Dr. Li’s 
26IWCC0138

24 WC 007653 
Page 2 
 
causation opinions have sufficiently proven causation, we find it unnecessary to also ascertain 
whether causation was supported or proven under a chain of events theory.  Accordingly, we strike 
the second to last paragraph on page 10 of the Arbitration Decision.  All else in the Arbitration 
Decision is affirmed and adopted. 
 
 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Decision of the 
Arbitrator filed July 8, 2025, is hereby affirmed and adopted with the change stated herein. 
 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that Respondent shall pay to 
Petitioner interest under §19(n) of the Act, if any. 
 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that Respondent shall have credit 
for all amounts paid, if any, to or on behalf of Petitioner on account of said accidental injury. 
 
[IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that this case be remanded to the 
Arbitrator for further proceedings consistent with this Decision. 
 
Pursuant to §19(f)(1) of the Act, this Decision and Opinion on Review of a claim against 
the State of Illinois is not subject to judicial Review.

An Application for Adjustment of Claim was filed in this matter, and a Notice of Hearing was mailed to each 
party.  The matter was heard by the Honorable Dennis O’Brien, Arbitrator of the Commission, in the city of 
Bloomington, on April 29, 2025.  After reviewing all of the evidence presented, the Arbitrator hereby makes 
findings on the disputed issues checked below, and attaches those findings to this document. 
 
DISPUTED ISSUES 
 
A. 
 Was Respondent operating under and subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation or Occupational  
 
 Diseases Act? 
 
B. 
 Was there an employee-employer relationship? 
 
C. 
 Did an accident occur that arose out of and in the course of Petitioner's employment by Respondent? 
 
D. 
 What was the date of the accident? 
 
E. 
 Was timely notice of the accident given to Respondent? 
 
F. 
 Is Petitioner's current condition of ill-being causally related to the injury? 
 
G.

H.

I. 
 What was Petitioner's marital status at the time of the accident? 
 
J.

 paid all appropriate charges for all reasonable and necessary medical services? 
 
K. 
 Is Petitioner entitled to any prospective medical care? 
 
L. 
 What temporary benefits are in dispute?

N.

FINDINGS 
 
On the date of accident, 11/8/2023, Respondent was operating under and subject to the provisions of the Act.   
 
On this date, an employee-employer relationship did exist between Petitioner and Respondent.   
 
On this date, Petitioner did sustain an accident that arose out of and in the course of employment. 
 
Timely notice of this accident was given to Respondent. 
 
Petitioner's current condition of ill-being is causally related to the accident. 
 
In the year preceding the injury, Petitioner earned $$84,211.13; the average weekly wage was $$1,598.77. 
 
On the date of accident, Petitioner was 58 years of age, married with 0 dependent children. 
 
Respondent has not paid all reasonable and necessary charges for all reasonable and necessary medical 
services.   
 
Respondent shall be given a credit of $0 for TTD, $0 for TPD, $0 for maintenance, and $0 for other benefits, 
for a total credit of $0. 
 
Respondent is entitled to a credit of $0 under Section 8(j) of the Act. 
 
ORDER 
 
 
   Petitioner’s medical conditions, left shoulder partial-thickness rotator cuff tear, impingement 
syndrome, AC joint dysfunction and biceps tenosynovitis and right shoulder partial-thickness rotator 
cuff tear, impingement syndrome, AC joint dysfunction and biceps tenosynovitis, are causally related to 
the accident of November 8, 2023.   
 
   All of the bills introduced into evidence in Petitioner Exhibit 3, pages 1 through 3, are related to 
Petitioner’s November 8, 2023 injury, are reasonable and were necessitated to treat or cure Petitioner’s 
injuries suffered in this accident, and are to be paid pursuant to Sections 8(a) and 8.2 of the Act.   
 
Respondent is entitled to credit for all portions of said medical bills which it has paid prior to the   
issuance of this decision. 
   Petitioner is entitled to prospective medical treatment as recommended by Dr. Li, to wit, bilateral 
shoulder arthroscopy with possible rotator cuff repair.   
 
 
 
 
In no instance shall this award be a bar to subsequent hearing and determination of an additional amount of 
medical benefits or compensation for a temporary or permanent disability, if any.   
 
RULES REGARDING APPEALS  Unless a party files a Petition for Review within 30 days after receipt of this decision, 
and perfects a review in accordance with the Act and Rules, then this decision shall be entered as the decision of 
the Commission.

Troy Aeschleman vs. Illinois Department of Transportation    24 WC 007653 
 
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
TESTIMONY AT ARBITRATION 
Petitioner   
 
Petitioner testified that he had been employed by Respondent as a highway maintainer since 2007. He 
said he also served as shop foreman or shop assistant for the past twelve years, a position that involved taking 
care of trucks and other equipment, and maintaining the yard, which involved going out and picking up debris 
on roadways. He said that as a highway maintainer he would perform on-the-roadway work to State roadways, 
including repairs to the road, mowing, filling of potholes, picking up trash, snow removal, etc.. He noted that as 
of the date of arbitration he was on medical leave for treatment of carpal tunnel on both of his hands, conditions 
not related to this accident. (TR 15,16) 
Petitioner testified that on November 8, 2023 he was the only person in the yard, and he got a call about a 
tractor part in a lane on I-55 southbound. When he got there he found it was a four foot by six foot cab roof 
from a tractor. He said traffic was bearing down, so he picked it up to drag it to the shoulder of the road. He 
decided to lift it over his head to get it into his one ton pickup truck, and while doing so he felt pain in both of 
this arms, causing him to put it down, then using the truck as leverage to put it in the truck. He said highway 
maintainers would be assigned to patrol the highways to find and pick up debris, usually working in a two 
person team. He said when that if a call came into the shop from headquarters passing on an Illinois State Police 
report of debris on a highway, Petitioner would go out to get it. (TR 16-18) 
Petitioner said that on the date of this accident, the Paris headquarters passed on such a report from the 
police, so he went out to retrieve that tractor part. He said this tractor cover was made of fiberglass on a steel 
frame, and it was pretty heavy, it took everything he had to get it into the truck. He said when he lifted it the 
piece made it to about chest high, he felt excruciating pain in his arms, and he could not get it all the way over 
his head. He testified that after putting it down, against the bed of the truck, he grabbed the bottom of it, used 
the truck as leverage, and slid it up, as he had to get it in there. He said he had an associate unload it for him, 
and he then went and talked to the lead worker, Adam Durbin, telling him what happened, and filled out an 
incident report, as he feared he had reaggravated a previous neck injury. (TR 19-22) 
Petitioner said he went home that day and took Tylenol or Ibuprofen for a week or so, treated it with ice, 
and just “babied it.” He said that since they were going into winter the work would not be as demanding, so he 
just self-care himself to make sure he did not reaggravate it. He said he used ice packs in the area between his 
neck and the outside of the shoulder areas, over the acromion and clavicular areas on a daily basis. He said he 
had different types of pain which would come and go, sometimes dull, achy or warm sensation, other times 
deep achy sensations, like a toothache, and other times stingy or shocking pain. The pain would last for varying 
amounts of time, sometimes five minutes, other times an hour or half a day. (TR 22-24) 
Petitioner testified that when he saw his family doctor for his annual physical, in February, he mentioned his 
pains to her, and she examined his arms. She advised him she did not have a solution, suggesting he see a 
26IWCC0138

5 
 
specialist for advice, though she did not recommend a doctor. He said he went to see Dr. Li on February 13, 
2024, and he told him of the November 8, 2023 incident where he lifted the piece of metal from a tractor into 
the back of his truck. Dr. Li had him undergo some MRI testing of both his left and his right shoulders. Dr. Li 
then had Petitioner receive physical therapy. He said he got physical therapy from March 2024 through June of 
2024, while continuing to work. He also had both shoulders injected, though neither the physical therapy nor the 
injections  helped the shoulders, though they helped his shoulder strength a little. (TR 25-29) 
Petitioner said Dr. Li gave him some work restrictions, but that was while he was being treated for carpal 
tunnel, and he was not allowed to climb or lift above his head, so he could no longer do the shop work or drive 
big trucks, as he would have to climb up into the big trucks. He said his work was limited to the one ton trucks.  
(TR 28-29)Petitioner said that while he thought he was doing all right in physical therapy, he would then go to 
work and perform his assigned work which caused him “to take two steps back.” He reported this to Dr. Li, and 
Dr. Li gave him different restrictions, no over chest activity with either arm, and no use of power tools. He said 
the restrictions were later changed to 25 pounds from 50 pounds. He said he continued to work until he had 
carpal tunnel surgery, just using smaller vehicles. (TR 29,30) 
Petitioner testified that physical therapy ended in June 2024, and Dr. Li recommended surgery as the MRI 
showed the tears were not getting better and the physical therapy and the injections had not worked. He said Dr. 
Li intended to perform the left shoulder surgery first, followed by the right shoulder surgery. He said he 
intended to have both surgeries. He said he had not received any physical therapy for his shoulders, that his 
shoulder symptoms were all right at present as long as he did not irritate them, that sleeping bothered them, that 
he had to change position while sleeping every two to three hours or they could get very bad. He said he did not 
really do anything, and he had been off work since Thanksgiving of 2024.  Prior to that time he was still having 
problems with his shoulders similar to the problem he had on the date of accident, a “stinger” or bad pain that 
would shoot down his arms, as well as soreness. He said he had trouble with some everyday activities, that 
putting on a sweatshirt was a struggle, as was opening curtains or putting anything on a top shelf. Even waving 
to a person with a hand up tweaked his shoulder. (TR 31-34) 
On cross examination, Petitioner said he recalled seeing Dr. Cohen in Joliet, that he was asked to move his 
arm to touch things, and he answered questions for the doctor. He agreed that he told Dr. Cohen that below 
shoulder height activities were tolerable. He said his shoulder pain varied, sometimes it was in one shoulder, 
sometimes in the other, it depended on which he was using the most. He said, and demonstrated, that his 
shooting pain started over the acromion and clavicular bones, at the AC joint on the outside of the shoulder, and 
went down towards the elbow. (TR 34-36) 
Petitioner agreed that he had recently had carpal tunnel releases in both arms, that his hands went to sleep 
less at night, but he still had soreness in his shoulders if he slept on his side. He said if he did something wrong, 
like lifting above his head or waving fast, those activities would cause shooting pains into his hands. (TR 37) 
 
MEDICAL EVIDENCE 
Petitioner was seen by Dr. Li (Orthopedic & Shoulder Center) on February 13, 2024.  Petitioner gave a 
history of bilateral shoulder pain after lifting a piece of metal from a tractor and throwing it overhead into his 
26IWCC0138

6 
 
truck on November 8, 2023.  He advised the doctor that he had not previously had an injury to the shoulders. He 
experienced numbness and tingling, especially at night, left worse than right, worsening with lifting overhead 
and improving with rest. X-rays revealed moderate narrowing of the right AC joint and type II acromion, and an 
old healed distal clavicle fracture on the left. Strength testing was 4 out of 5 for supraspinatus and external 
rotation strength. He had a positive Neer and Hawkins impingement tests, positive biceps load test, O'Brien's 
test, and crossarm adduction test. Petitioner also made hand complaints which he noted had been present for 
many years, but which were getting worse. Dr. Li diagnosed both bilateral rotator cuff injuries as well as 
bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. MRIs of both shoulders were ordered. (PX 2 p.3-10) 
The MRIs were performed on February 15, 2024 and February 20, 2024, and showed subacromial 
impingement, low to moderate grade articular and bursal surface tears of the supraspinatus tendon and 
infraspinatus tendon. The left shoulder MRI showed a partial thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon, no 
high-grade tear of the supraspinatus, but a low-grade partial thickness tearing of the superior subscapularis 
insertion. (PX 2 p.17-20) 
Dr. Li saw Petitioner on March 5, 2024. His interpretation of the MRIs was consistent with that of the 
radiologist’s. Petitioner’s symptoms remained the same, as did Dr. Li’s physical examination findings. Dr. Li 
scheduled Petitioner for corticosteroid injections in the subacromial space of both shoulders, which were 
performed on March 6 and 7, 2024, and ordered physical therapy. (PX 2 p.11- 16,21,22) 
Petitioner began physical therapy for both shoulders on March 12, 2024. During his physical therapy 
sessions, he made gradual improvements in some areas, such as passive range of motion, but he continued to 
have pain and functional limitations. His final therapy visit was on July 2, 2024, and at that time he was 
reporting pain of 3/10, and the therapist noted Petitioner continued to have limited functionality secondary to 
decreased strength, decreased range of motion, and increased pain. (PX 2 p. 23-43, 49-80, 86-98) 
On April 15, 2024, Petitioner advised Dr. Li that the corticosteroid injections improved his pain about 40 % 
for two weeks, after which the pain slowly returned. Petitioner said the physical therapy had improved his range 
of motion, but not his pain, as he was still having pain with reaching up as well as when raising his arms. 
Petitioner was restricted from doing over chest work or using power tools. (PX 2 p.44-48) 
On May 3, 2024, Petitioner was examined at Respondent’s request by Dr. Cohen. Dr. Cohen issued a report 
in regard to that examination, summarizing the history given to him by Petitioner, the medical records of 
Petitioner’s treatment through March 7, 2024, and medical records relating to Petitioner’s unrelated carpal 
tunnel syndromes. He described his physical examination findings relating to the shoulders, with findings that 
were not compatible with those of Dr. Li, such as 5/5 rotator cuff strength with pain, and a negative crossover 
test bilaterally. He interpreted x-rays taken in his office on the date of this examination as showing evidence of 
AC arthritis, glenohumeral arthritis, and a type 2 acromion, as well as evidence of a prior clavicle fracture and 
calcification along the coraclavicular ligaments. He felt Petitioner’s accident could have caused bilateral 
shoulder strains and possibly some cervical radiculopathy, which had totally resolved by the time he examined 
him. He felt this accident temporarily exacerbated Petitioner’s underlying arthritic symptomatology.  He 
acknowledged that as of the date of his exam Petitioner’s main problem was pain while lifting overhead. Dr. 
Cohen thought the medical treatment he had received through the date he examined him was reasonable and 
appropriate and related to the accident of November 8, 2023. He believed two to four weeks of work 
26IWCC0138

7 
 
conditioning would allow Petitioner to regain his overhead lifting function. He did not believe Petitioner was at 
maximum medical improvement. (RX 2 p.1-5 
When seen by Dr. Li on June 6, 2024, Petitioner reported that his left shoulder pain was worse, and his 
physical therapy was helping with his range of motion, but not the pain. He advised Dr. Li that he had 
undergone an IME appointment, but did not have the report. Dr. Li’s examination findings of that date showed 
decrease supraspinatus and external rotation strength, and four positive orthopedic tests of the shoulders. Dr. Li 
continued Petitioner’s restrictions. (PX 2 p.81-85) 
On July 10, 2024, Petitioner advised Dr. Li that while he had been working with physical therapy, both of 
his shoulders were still bothering him significantly. Dr. Li noted that both Petitioner’s shoulders had failed 
nonoperative treatment consisting of corticosteroid injection, NSAIDs and therapy, and that the left shoulder 
was more symptomatic. He stated that he would get authorization for a left shoulder arthroscopy and possible 
rotator cuff repair. Physical therapy was discontinued at this point. Petitioner’s prior restrictions were to 
continue, with the added restriction that he was not to lift, push or pull more than 50 pounds. (PX 2 p. 99-104) 
Dr. Li saw Petitioner on August 13, 2024, with Petitioner reporting that both of his shoulders continued to 
bother him significantly. Petitioner continued to work with restrictions. Dr. Li reported that Petitioner’s left 
shoulder arthroscopy had not been approved by workers’ compensation at that time. He continued Petitioner’s 
restrictions of no over chest work no lifting, pushing or pulling over 50 pounds, and no use of power tools. (PX 
2 p.105-110) 
Dr. Cohen issued a supplemental records review report on September 18, 2024.  He reviewed records, 
including Dr. Li’s July 10, 2024 office notes. He noted that Petitioner had not undergone the work conditioning 
/ work hardening he had recommended. He said that while he had expected Petitioner would be at maximum 
medical improvement by the time of the writing of this report, based on Dr. Li’s office notes, he could not state 
that Petitioner was at maximum medical improvement, though he still recommended the work conditioning / 
work hardening.  He said his prior opinions had not been changed by the additional records he had reviewed. 
(RX 4p.1-3)  
Dr. Cohen issued another supplemental records review report on October 25, 2024, after reviewing imaging 
discs which had been forwarded to him. He said he saw no evidence of a rotator cuff tear in either the right 
shoulder or the left shoulder MRI imaging, though there was evidence of biceps tendinitis and rotator cuff 
tendinitis in both shoulders. HE said his review of these images did not change his opinions as stated in the 
prior two reports. (RX 5 p.1) 
Petitioner was again seen by Dr. Li on September 17, 2024 and November 12, 2024. Petitioner advised him 
that he continued to work with the restrictions which had issued, and his shoulders continued to hurt him at 
times while at work, but he said the pain was tolerable. On both of those occasions it was noted that 
authorization for the surgery had not yet been received, and. Petitioner’s physical examination findings were 
unchanged. They were continuing to wait for surgery authorization for the shoulders. His restrictions were 
continued. (PX 2 p.111-120) 
 
 
26IWCC0138

8 
 
DEPOSITION TESTIMONY OF DR. LAWRENCE LI 
Dr. Li testified that he is a board-certified orthopedic surgeon with over 30 years experience diagnosing and 
treating orthopedic injuries. Dr. Li said he first saw Petitioner on February 13, 2024, taking a history from 
Petitioner in regard to his job maintaining roads. Petitioner told him of the November 8, 2023 incident where he 
lifted a piece of metal from a tractor overhead, at which time he felt pain in both shoulders. He told Dr. Li his 
symptoms were worse at night and his left shoulder was worse than his right. Dr. Li testified that at this initial 
appointment Petitioner had a slightly decreased range of motion and moderately decreased strength, as well as 
positive Neer and Hawkins impingement tests, suggesting rotator cuff pathology. He also found Petitioner to 
have a positive biceps load test and O'Brien's test, consistent with labral pathology. Petitioner also appeared to 
have pain over the AC joint. Dr. Li recommended bilateral shoulder MRI’s. (PX 4 p. 1,6-8)   
The MRIs were performed, and Dr. Li testified that the right shoulder MRI revealed a moderate grade 
articular surface and bursal surface tear of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendon, subacromial bursitis, and 
AC joint arthritis. He said the left MRI shoulder showed partial tears of the supraspinatus tendon and biceps 
tendinosis, AC joint arthropathy, and perhaps a posterior superior labral tear. (PX 4 p. 9) 
Dr. Li said that at his next appointment with Petitioner, on March 5, 2024, he discussed the MRI findings 
with Petitioner, and recommended corticosteroid injections and physical therapy. (PX 4 p. 8, 10) 
Dr. Li testified that on April 15, 2024, Petitioner told him that the corticosteroid injections improved his 
pain about 40 percent, for about two weeks, but then the pain slowly came back. He also reported that physical 
therapy helped him with his range of motion, but not decrease his pain, that he had pain with reaching up, as 
well as raising his arm. Dr. Li testified that these complaints were consistent with rotator cuff tears. (PX 4 p. 8, 
10) 
On June 6, 2024, Petitioner advised him that his left shoulder pain was worsening. Dr. Li noted that the 
therapy had helped Petitioner’s range of motion but he was still having pain. Dr. Li’s physical exam revealed 
Petitioner to have nearly full range of motion, but he did not have very good strength and still had the positive 
provocative testing, Neer and Hawkins impingement, biceps load test, and O'Brien's test. (PX 4 p. 14-15) 
Dr. Li said Petitioner continued to complain of significant shoulder pain when seen on July 10, 2024 
appointment. Dr. Li said that during this appointment he discontinued physical therapy, and recommended left 
shoulder surgery, as Petitioner had failed conservative treatment for both shoulders, injections, medications, and 
therapy. HE said he therefore recommended a left shoulder arthroscopy and rotator cuff repair, noting he could 
only perform one surgery at a time. He said he would request the right shoulder surgery once the left shoulder 
was getting close to being done. (PX 4 p. 15,16,20-22) 
Dr. Li testified that in his opinion Petitioner’s November 8, 2023 accident caused a permanent aggravation 
and acceleration to Petitioner’s rotator cuff tendon tears, and it also affected his AC joint disease. Dr. Li said he 
disagreed with the statements in the IME report opining that Petitioner would regain his function with four 
weeks of work conditioning, noting that Petitioner had already received approximately twelve to sixteen weeks 
of therapy, and had not regained his overhead use. (PX 4 p. 26) 
On cross examination Dr. Li testified that he had reviewed Dr. Cohen’s report, noted that Dr. Cohen 
believed Petitioner’s problems were arthritis and tendinitis in both shoulders, but while he agreed Petitioner had 
26IWCC0138

9 
 
those conditions, he felt he had more problems than tendinitis, he had tears in his rotator cuff tendons. He felt 
both of Petitioner’s shoulders had moderate supraspinatus tendon tears, and that during physical examination 
testing he was found to have positive tests. He said his steroid injections produced a 40 percent reduction in 
pain, which supported his diagnosis, that is the expected experience of relief when there is pathology in the 
rotator cuff tendon. He said the positive biceps load test and O’Brien’s test were suggestive of labral pathology, 
bilaterally. He said he felt Petitioner’s main shoulder issues involved the rotator cuff, that problems with labral 
and biceps pain could be addressed with a subpectoral biceps tenodesis procedure while repairing the rotator 
cuff.  (PX 4 p.32-35) 
Dr. Li said that twelve to sixteen weeks after his first shoulder surgery, Petitioner would be recovered to the 
point where he was ready for the second shoulder’s surgery.  (PX 4 p.36) 
 
DEPOSITION OF DR. MICHAEL COHEN 
Dr. Cohen testified that he is a board-certified in orthopedic surgery. Dr. Cohen said he examined Petitioner 
on May 3, 2024 at the request of Respondent. His report was entered into evidence as Exhibit 4. (RX 3, p. 5,6) 
Dr. Cohen’s testimony in regard to history, complaints, physical examination findings and record reviews 
was consistent with his medical reports of May 3, September 18, and October 25, 2024, above. 
Dr. Cohen testified that on physical examination of Petitioner’s shoulders, he had symmetric abduction of 
160 degrees and full internal and external rotation, negative impingement signs, full rotator cuff strength, no AC 
joint symptomatology or provocative signs for a labral tear. Dr. Cohen diagnosed Petitioner with bilateral 
shoulder sprain and recommended two to four weeks of work conditioning to address the pain and overhead 
strength. He said he did not believe Petitioner had reached maximum medical improvement, as shown by his 
recommending work conditioning for the shoulders. (RX 3 p. 7-9) 
Dr. Cohen noted that after reviewing additional medical records and the MRI images of Petitioner’s 
shoulders, he was of the opinion that bilateral rotator cuff surgery was not warranted for Petitioner. He agreed 
that there were occasions when an MRI did not show a tear, but that was not common. (RX 3 p.13) 
On cross examination, Dr. Cohen acknowledged that Petitioner had had physical therapy but that he did not 
the amount of physical therapy he received, he did not recall if the physical therapy records had been provided 
to him, those records could have been relevant.  He said Petitioner did advise him that physical therapy had only 
improved his symptoms about 20 percent. He stated that it was possible for people with rotator cuff tears to 
have improved range of motion with physical therapy, and still experience pain. (RX 3, p. 18-20,29,25) 
 
ARBITRATOR CREDIBILITY ASSESSMENT 
Petitioner’s testimony was consistent with the medical records contemporaneous to the time of the injury. 
No contradictory evidence was submitted at arbitration in regard to how the accident occurred, his reporting of 
it, and his subsequent medical treatment.  Petitioner answered all questions asked by both attorneys in a 
straightforward manner, with no apparent attempt to be evasive in his testimony.  The Arbitrator finds Petitioner 
to have been a credible witness.

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW: 
In support of the Arbitrator’s decision relating to whether Petitioner’s current conditions of ill-being, left 
shoulder partial-thickness rotator cuff tear, impingement syndrome, AC joint dysfunction and biceps 
tenosynovitis and right shoulder partial-thickness rotator cuff tear, impingement syndrome, AC joint

Arbitrator makes the following findings: 
The findings of fact, above, are incorporated herein. 
The summaries of medical evidence and deposition testimony, above, are incorporated herein. 
The findings in regard to credibility assessment, above, are incorporated herein. 
The histories given by Petitioner to his treating physicians, his complaints to those medical providers, and the 
test results obtained while being treated all are consistent with Petitioner’s testimony in regard to the accident 
and the physical complaints he suffered following the accident. Respondent stipulated that Petitioner suffered 
an accident on November 8, 2023.  
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner’s medical conditions, left shoulder partial-thickness rotator cuff tear, 
impingement syndrome, AC joint dysfunction and biceps tenosynovitis and right shoulder partial-
thickness rotator cuff tear, impingement syndrome, AC joint dysfunction and biceps tenosynovitis, are 
causally related to the accident of November 8, 2023.  This finding is based upon the testimony of Petitioner, 
the medical records herein, and the deposition testimony of Dr. Li. The Arbitrator gives greater weight to the 
opinions of Dr. Li to those of Dr. Cohen due to his having seen and examined Petitioner on numerous 
occasions, as opposed to Dr. Cohen’s one examination, his having ordered and followed Petitioner’s physical 
therapy treatments, as opposed to Dr. Cohen not even being sure he saw those records, and Dr. Li’s having 
exhausted several conservative treatment regimens prior to recommending surgery due to the failure of those 
conservative treatments.  
The Arbitrator further finds that the chain-of-events also support a finding of causal connection.  This 
finding is based upon Petitioner’s unrebutted testimony to a pre-accident state of asymptomatic good health in 
the right shoulder, her having an accident on July 16, 2020 and her immediately after said accident having 
sudden pain, medical treatment and new diagnoses based on diagnostic testing and physical examinations.
